CHIEF COMPLAINT
Elevated blood sugar

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
55-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with significantly elevated blood sugar requiring treatment. Patient attributes this to recent travel, hosting visitors over the past couple of weeks, not monitoring sugar intake, and stress. Patient was started on metformin in the emergency room. Patient reports feeling well since the ER visit. Prior hemoglobin A1Cs were noted to be borderline, but current level is elevated. Regarding anxiety, patient notes that the recent hyperglycemic episode did not help his anxiety symptoms, though he reports his anxiety has been better as the weekend approaches and feels things are now under control. Regarding seizures, patient denies any seizures for several months; his most recent seizure was minor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Denies recent fever or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety
Epilepsy

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Keppra

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent travel and hosting visitors over the past couple of weeks associated with stress. Was not monitoring sugar intake during this time.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs appear normal. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear. Trace pitting edema noted to lower extremities, likely secondary to fluid retention from emergency room IV fluids.

RESULTS
Blood glucose: 162 mg/dL (checked approximately 2 hours after last meal)
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0 (prior value approximately 6.0)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus:
- Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily with consideration for dose increase over time
- Order hemoglobin A1C for future monitoring

Anxiety:
- Discussed potential seasonal concerns and issues leading into winter
- Patient willing to try new treatment

Epilepsy:
- Continue Keppra
- Patient to follow up with neurologist (last seen approximately 3 months ago)
